title: Source: src/agent_runtime/tasks
summary: File ownership, boundaries, state and collaborators.

Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/tasks

src/agent_runtime/tasks/init.py

Python · Tier A

Durable Agent UI task records.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/dependencies.py

Python · Tier A

Share top-level task edge parsing and deterministic eligibility between RAM and retained SQL repositories. evaluate_rows computes waiting/blocked/satisfied projections from immutable task intent and explicit per-edge waivers. The SQL helpers validate and record edges inside the caller transaction, while memory_dependencies owns RAM writes. This layer never executes tasks or invents success for a failed prerequisite.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
reject 26 Raise a localized LaneConflict carrying the stable dependency diagnostic code, so creation and recovery callers can present the same failure identity.
edges 35 Decode a task's stored JSON or thaw its RAM edge array, require a list and validate each TaskDependency before returning normalized detached dictionaries. Malformed history raises rather than implying no dependency.
validate 48 Walk proposed prerequisite edges and their ancestors inside the caller's SQL transaction. Reject self/duplicate edges, missing or cross-conversation targets, corrupt upstream arrays and cycles before saving creation intent.
record_event 94 Append a dependency checkpoint in the existing SQL task journal using a unique negative trace- event ID, localized title and serialized transition details; the caller owns commit/rollback.
register_requested_dependency 122 Resolve an explicit selected task or the immediately previous task in creation order, rejecting conflicting selection modes. Validate the edge and assign immutable creation sequence in the caller's writer transaction, then refresh eligibility and record registration/immediate satisfaction.
candidates 173 Read live, unarchived tasks in one conversation ordered by creation identity, including queued and active interaction waits. This selector does not filter dependency eligibility or apply a history limit; columns is an internal SQL projection argument.
evaluate 185 Load task and per-edge skip rows from the supplied SQL view and delegate to the shared pure graph evaluator. The returned eligibility projections do not mutate native execution outcomes.
evaluate_rows 205 Derive satisfied, waiting or blocked eligibility from task rows and recorded edge waivers, memoizing ancestor visits. Missing, deleted, wrong-scope, corrupt or cyclic prerequisites fail closed; a completed direct target satisfies its edge. The function only returns projections and does not start or reopen tasks.
refresh 286 Save changed SQL eligibility projections, emit transition checkpoints only for queued tasks whose dependency state changed, and bump their lane versions. Finished/cancelled tasks are never reactivated by recomputation.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/lanes.py

Python · Tier A

Own standalone SQL transactions for conversation submissions, future queue order, explicit dependencies and durable request/attempt bindings. Enqueue deduplicates client intent, reservation commits identity before native dispatch, and recovery revalidates parent/status/capacity. Lane projections explain why queued work waits; explicit start/stop/skip actions persist narrow dependency decisions. Retention and deletion preserve submission/request tombstones. Native RunStore supplies execution truth and the queue coordinator delivers cancellation/recovery; this module does not run model turns or external commands.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
now 66 Timestamp lane transitions and accepted identities with a timezone-aware UTC ISO string, using the same representation as task storage.
lane_id 72 Derive a stable fixed-length lane key from the complete conversation ID, avoiding the legacy queue-lane length bound without truncating user identity.
LaneConflict 77 The client intent conflicts with authoritative lane state.
ConversationTaskLanes 88 Implement SQL transactions for accepted chat intent, ordering, dependency-aware eligibility and request/attempt bindings. Native workers, physical/model capacity and cancellation effects have separate owners; submission and request identities survive task-history deletion.
ConversationTaskLanes.update_future_chat_runtime_guard_policy 90 Narrow post-admission edit in the caller's attached-store transaction. Caller holds task_queue_lock then the task-store lock, and attaches the task database as completion_tasks before BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Reservation uses that same queue lock/SQLite writer boundary. Submission digests and all unrelated context remain immutable.
ConversationTaskLanes.submission 212 Look up the durable client-submission identity and require its saved digest to match the requested or explicitly compatible digest. A conflict raises LaneConflict even if task history has already been removed; absence returns None.
ConversationTaskLanes.enqueue_chat 229 Commit a deduplicated submission, accepted task/context, immutable creation/dependency identity and lane revision together. Optional composer/admission callbacks join attached databases inside the writer transaction; failures roll everything back. Limit queued rows to 32 and, for an imported bound request, commit its attempt/binding before returning. Matching retries reuse existing intent; consumed identities cannot resurrect missing history.
ConversationTaskLanes.chat_request_binding 411 Read the immutable request-to-task/attempt/lane identity retained for acceptance and recovery. Return None when absent; a surviving binding does not guarantee that visible task history still exists.
ConversationTaskLanes.task_lane 423 Build a consistent SQL read projection containing bounded history plus all live/blocked tasks, editable future tasks and dependency candidates. Compute queue reasons with the reservation eligibility helpers, expose pending preparations, and include a selected historical dependency even outside the history page. Compact mode omits captured context; run_next_available remains a compatibility field set to False.
ConversationTaskLanes.eligible_chat_heads 591 Return candidate heads from one read transaction using the same dependency/capacity policy as reservation. These are scheduling observations; another writer can change eligibility before reserve_chat_attempt commits a binding.
ConversationTaskLanes.can_continue_chat 613 Project whether task-level continuation gates permit the requested restart/follow- up/authority-renewal mode. This read-only result does not establish that native work has settled and cannot replace reservation-time validation.
ConversationTaskLanes.reopen_failed_request 637 Under the caller's queue lock, revalidate the latest failed request and reclaim its existing attempt/task as running for explicit compiler retry. Preserve identity, require dependency/capacity eligibility and clear stale outcome previews; check_only performs admission without mutation, while an already-running accepted retry is idempotent.
ConversationTaskLanes.reserve_chat_attempt 700 Atomically validate future or recovery intent, runtime admission, preparation readiness, dependencies and lane capacity before creating an attempt and request binding. Duplicate ordinary claims return the current attempt. Replacement continuations must name the latest parent; they settle the replaced attempt and preserve logical task/creation identity. Retry may allocate a new Agent journal, while continuation retains its accepted journal. No native worker starts here.
ConversationTaskLanes.edit_chat 873 Change only a future task's prompt/title and optional parameter snapshot under the writer transaction. Invalidate prepared compiler output when either source changes, bump the lane revision and reinitialize runtime admission; immutable submission identity and dependency edges remain intact.
ConversationTaskLanes.remove_chat 913 Cancel and archive one never-started task instead of erasing its submission identity. Refresh dependent tasks and lane revision so a lost-response retry cannot recreate removed intent and descendants see the cancelled prerequisite.
ConversationTaskLanes.clear_chat_queue 934 Cancel/archive queued conversation rows with no attempt history, refresh dependencies and increment the lane revision. Started work and durable submission identities survive; this operation is not a native cancellation request.
ConversationTaskLanes.reorder_chat 958 Require the observed lane revision and an exact permutation of every future queued task. Temporarily negate positions to avoid unique-index collisions, then reassign the existing positions in the requested order. Creation sequence, accepted dependency targets and prepared source identity are unchanged.
ConversationTaskLanes.run_next_chat 999 Retain the old entry point without allowing an implicit failure/dependency bypass: report no- next-item for an empty queue and otherwise reject the request. Automatic scheduling follows explicit dependency eligibility.
ConversationTaskLanes.start_blocked_chat 1011 Record an explicit manual-start waiver for each validated dependency of one blocked future task after checking the lane revision. Preserve the edges and append a checkpoint describing the decision; capacity, runtime admission and actual dispatch remain separate gates.
ConversationTaskLanes._next_after_failed_locked 1054 Offer only the immediate later future task for an eligible failed/stalled latest request. Reject repeated request-specific skips and missing/cross-conversation prerequisites; every other prerequisite must already be completed. Return the exact next-task identity and lane revision for subsequent compare-and-commit.
ConversationTaskLanes.next_after_failed_request 1103 Read a possible next-task decision for the latest failed chat attempt without mutating its outcome or waiving dependencies. The returned revision must be checked again when the user confirms advancement.
ConversationTaskLanes.next_after_stalled_request 1108 Native admission must separately prove that this attempt has settled.
ConversationTaskLanes.advance_stalled_request 1119 With the caller's queue lock, attach native storage and commit a stop/skip decision only after rechecking task/version, settled native status, pending work, live ownership and continuation absence. Release exactly the selected predecessor edge, or defer release until a requested Stop summary finishes. Persisted intent lets reconciliation finish cancellation after a crash; this transaction itself launches no cancellation or model work.
ConversationTaskLanes.release_summary_advance 1210 Finish a previously committed Stop-with-summary decision only when native state is terminal. Clear its pending-release flag, insert the selected dependency waiver once, append the task checkpoint and refresh eligibility in the same attached-store transaction; return False before finalization or on repeat calls.
ConversationTaskLanes.continue_after_failed_request 1255 Revalidate the selected next task and lane revision, then persist a request-specific waiver and activity checkpoint for one failed predecessor. Preserve its recorded outcome and dependency edge; unrelated prerequisites remain effective.
ConversationTaskLanes.assert_chat_deletable 1290 Reject ordinary conversation deletion while unarchived queued/active/interrupted intent, a lane blocker or pending steering remains. This preflight performs no cancellation and does not replace the manager's broader cross-store lifecycle checks.
ConversationTaskLanes.delete_chat_lane 1320 After deletion preflight, clear internal chat dependency edges and remove task-owned history plus the lane in a writer transaction. Submission and request-binding tombstones survive; native history, scratch scopes and external effects belong to separate lifecycle owners.
ConversationTaskLanes.abandon_chat_lane_for_management 1344 Within the caller's transaction, archive abandoned chat intent, interrupt unresolved started attempts, cancel never-started work and reject pending amendments before removing the lane. Keep completed outcomes, execution evidence and submission identities; external effects may remain unknown and cancellation delivery occurs elsewhere.
ConversationTaskLanes.delete_chat_lane_for_management 1392 Join the conversation manager's transaction and validate every chat task before removing lane/task rows. Only an explicitly authorized option discards genuinely unstarted queued intent; unresolved work, bindings and pending amendments otherwise protect deletion. Clear internal edges first and retain submission/request tombstones so retries cannot replay deleted intent.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/memory_dependencies.py

Python · Tier A

Own top-level task prerequisite transitions in the active RAM transaction. MemoryDependencies validates creation intent, maintains dependency checkpoints and revisits affected descendants plus their ancestors through shared graph evaluation. The mixin relies on MemoryTaskStore inserts/lane versions and TaskRecords reverse indexes; it does not dispatch work, alter native Activity graphs or waive unrelated dependencies.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
MemoryDependencies 21 Add top-level prerequisite validation and incremental eligibility updates to MemoryTaskStore. Methods use the caller's active Records view; they own task intent and lane projections, not native Activity execution or model context.
MemoryDependencies._refresh_dependencies 70 Follow the reverse dependency index from changed tasks to affected descendants, evaluate that subgraph with its ancestors and update only changed projections. Queued state transitions emit checkpoints and affected lanes receive version bumps without automatically starting work.
MemoryDependencies._validate_dependencies 109 Validate proposed edge models and walk upstream tasks in the same transaction. Reject self references, duplicate targets, absent/corrupt nodes, cross-conversation links and cycles with stable LaneConflict codes.
MemoryDependencies._register_dependency 149 Resolve explicit or previous-task creation intent using the conversation's ordered index, assign its creation sequence, validate/store the edge and refresh eligibility. Record registration and already-satisfied edges in the same task publication; conflicting intent modes reject.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/memory_lanes.py

Python · Tier A

Own conversation task ordering, replay bindings and recovery transitions on Controller RAM. MemoryLanes composes with MemoryTaskStore and its dependency/preparation helpers; read operations share a snapshot and writes publish through the hub. Admission stores intent and outbox notices, while the conversation coordinator starts native work and delivers steering. Revision, retirement and dependency guards reject stale transitions; request bindings survive deletion to prevent identity reuse.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
conflict 22 Create a localized lane conflict while preserving optional machine codes and conflict metadata supplied by the caller.
MemoryLanes 29 Compose conversation queue operations into MemoryTaskStore. Repository decorators reuse one hub view/transaction; this mixin owns lane order, task/request bindings, recovery gates and explicit dependency waivers, while the coordinator owns native execution and notifications.
MemoryLanes.update_future_chat_runtime_guard_policy 44 Within the caller’s policy transaction, retarget only queued chat tasks with no attempt history and a live lane. Record one shared action identity with per-task checkpoints, then bump affected lane versions; running or previously attempted work retains its accepted policy.
MemoryLanes.eligible_chat_heads 243 Expose detached task models for currently eligible lane heads from one read snapshot; selecting a head does not reserve or start an attempt.
MemoryLanes.submission 249 Look up a client submission and require its saved digest to match the current or explicitly accepted compatibility digests. Return a detached record, or None for a new identity.
MemoryLanes.enqueue_chat 260 Atomically bind a submission digest to one chat task, sequence, dependency intent and pending notice. Replay returns the existing task; fresh admission checks capacity/legacy bindings and can join conversation/profile callbacks on the same hub. Initialize parameter holds before returning; no model is launched here.
MemoryLanes.pending_admissions 396 Read existing tasks whose acceptance notice is still pending in the Controller outbox; vanished task rows cannot manufacture replay work.
MemoryLanes.acknowledge_admission 406 Delete a task’s outbox notice after the coordinator publishes it. Repeated acknowledgement is harmless and does not change the task’s execution status.
MemoryLanes.saved_submission_context 412 Recover a detached accepted context through the submission-to-task binding for idempotent replay; absent submissions or removed tasks return None.
MemoryLanes.admission_fence 421 Read settings, conversation capability/permission, Gateway and parameter admission revisions from one shared transaction view. Callers compare this tuple before committing work captured outside that view.
MemoryLanes.reconciliation_tasks 438 Collect active chat tasks and unarchived failed/cancelled/interrupted tasks with attempts for native reconciliation. Completed history is not scanned as runnable recovery intent.
MemoryLanes.active_chat_request_ids 455 Return active chat request identities in stable creation order for one conversation; tasks without a current request are omitted.
MemoryLanes.open_request_ids 469 Return current request IDs, falling back to task IDs, for unarchived open work. Exclude never-started admission holds so parameter clarification does not occupy an execution slot.
MemoryLanes.pending_steers 486 Return detached pending steering records for the coordinator’s idempotent delivery pass.
MemoryLanes.settle_steer 493 Settle only a pending delivery as delivered or rejected. Rejection restores a steered task to the queue only while its lane still exists, then refreshes dependencies; late acknowledgements do not reopen retired lanes.
MemoryLanes.chat_request_binding 513 Read the durable request-to-task/attempt binding, including retained idempotency tombstones whose task may have been removed.
MemoryLanes.task_lane 521 Assemble a lane view from its newest 100 unarchived ordered tasks plus queued, active and designated blocked rows. Include editable queue order, projected blockers and dependency choices; compact mode strips execution context. This display may exceed 100 rows and does not grant dispatch authority.
MemoryLanes.can_continue_chat 634 Select the allowed prior states for ordinary continuation, restart, follow-up or authority renewal and evaluate the shared continuation gate without changing state.
MemoryLanes.reopen_failed_request 652 Validate the latest bound attempt and dependency/capacity gates before restoring a failed request to running. check_only performs validation; an already-running task is unchanged. Retired bindings cannot create a replacement task.
MemoryLanes.reserve_chat_attempt 708 Reserve one request identity and running attempt transactionally after preparation, admission, dependency, capacity and recovery checks. Repeated active/renewal claims reuse their attempt; replacement flags require the latest parent. Retain request tombstones and rotate retry journals without starting native execution.
MemoryLanes.edit_chat 832 Edit only never-started queued intent, replacing its title and optional parameter snapshot. Changed prompt/bindings invalidate compiler preparation; lane version and admission status are refreshed in the same transaction.
MemoryLanes.remove_chat 866 Cancel and archive one editable future task, retaining its submission identity and propagating dependency changes.
MemoryLanes.clear_chat_queue 876 Cancel/archive queued chat tasks with no attempt history, then refresh their descendants and lane revision. Previously attempted work is preserved.
MemoryLanes.reorder_chat 899 Require the current lane version and an exact permutation of all unarchived queued tasks. Reassign their existing positions only after each passes the unstarted-task guard; dependency identities and creation order remain unchanged.
MemoryLanes.run_next_chat 921 Retain the legacy read-only entry point: report an empty queue or reject implicit dependency bypass. Dispatch uses eligible heads or explicit per-task release instead.
MemoryLanes.start_blocked_chat 930 Require the current lane version and a blocked unstarted task, validate its dependency edges, then record explicit manual-start waivers and a dependency event. Normal capacity/admission checks still apply when an attempt is reserved.
MemoryLanes.next_after_failed_request 1009 Project the versioned successor choice for a failed latest request without mutating its dependency edges.
MemoryLanes.next_after_stalled_request 1015 Project the same explicit successor choice for eligible active, interrupted, cancelled or failed work; the caller must still validate native ownership before advancing.
MemoryLanes.continue_after_failed_request 1047 Revalidate the exact successor and lane version, then record the user’s failed-predecessor waiver. A stale selection raises instead of releasing different work.
MemoryLanes.advance_stalled_request 1063 Join task and native-run state on one hub, require a supported stalled status without pending work, current owner or continuation, and save the explicit skip/stop decision. Stop-with- summary delays dependency release; other actions publish the waiver immediately.
MemoryLanes.release_summary_advance 1115 After a native run reaches a terminal state, clear its pending summary-release flag and publish the saved successor waiver atomically. Repeated or premature calls return False.
MemoryLanes.assert_chat_deletable 1142 Reject synchronous lane removal while unarchived queued/active/interrupted chat work, a lane blocker or a pending steer remains. This guard does not perform cancellation or filesystem cleanup.
MemoryLanes.delete_chat_lane 1166 After the deletability guard, clear chat dependency edges, delete each chat task through the protected store helper and remove the lane. Request/submission tombstones remain available for replay fencing.
MemoryLanes.abandon_chat_lane 1183 Retire local lane ownership by archiving chat tasks, interrupting unsettled attempts, clearing current pointers and rejecting pending steers. Preserve known terminal statuses and request bindings; this bookkeeping does not establish remote cancellation.
MemoryLanes.remove_chat_for_management 1238 Validate every chat row before synchronous management removal, optionally accepting only truly unstarted queued work for discard. Reject unresolved lane/current/steering ownership; then remove edges and records through the store’s deletion guard. Active asynchronous collection has a separate owner.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/memory_preparations.py

Python · Tier A

Implement the same private preparation protocol on Controller RAM authority. MemoryPreparations uses task repository read/operation decorators to claim one source, publish state under an 8 MiB serialized limit and consume only through a live request/attempt binding. Source identity is checked again in the save transaction; stale, cancelled or deleted records cannot accept late compiler output. Shared import validation preserves policy and model provenance. TaskRecords owns related deletion/cancellation hooks, and checkpoints serialize these native JSON records for recovery.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
MemoryPreparations 29 Compose preparation claims, source checks, saves and consumption into the Controller task repository. Read decorators share an immutable view; operation decorators publish repeatable state changes atomically. JSON-shaped state remains native RAM data until checkpoint serialization, and no live SQL or inference occurs here.
MemoryPreparations.get_preparation 44 Read one explicit task-owned ID or the current task-contract row from the same snapshot. An ID belonging to another task returns None rather than crossing ownership.
MemoryPreparations.claim_preparation 77 Reserve one generating record for eligible future chat intent after parameter-admission checks. Reuse a current matching identity without another compiler owner; otherwise invalidate it and allocate the next source revision in the same optimistic publication.
MemoryPreparations.save_preparation 184 Enter the atomic task repository operation and repeat the source check within the save itself; a preceding read-only check cannot authorize publication.
MemoryPreparations.preparation_current 190 Read current source eligibility and preparation identity from one immutable task view without reserving or changing the record.
MemoryPreparations.consume_preparation 198 Atomically validate the active request/attempt/lane binding and exact conversation/prompt, then use the shared snapshot/provenance validator. Preserve the first consuming request identity for idempotent restart and approved retry lineage; absence keeps the legacy on- demand path available.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/memory_records.py

Python · Tier A

Adapt the existing task schema to Controller RAM authority and maintain derived indexes. operation/read scope composed repository methods to one immutable view or optimistic publication; TaskRecords discovers restore schemas and updates creation/lane order, reverse prerequisites, timing, retention and native capacity signals. SQLite initialization supports restore/checkpoint generations; runtime consumers use Records rather than connections.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
operation 54 Decorate a task repository method with an atomic write or immutable read scope. Nested calls reuse the thread-local transaction; outer writes may retry and therefore must contain only repeatable state computations.
read 87 Apply operation's read-only variant so composed task queries share one immutable repository view without opening SQL or publishing state.
initialize 94 Initialize the legacy version-7 task schema for restore/checkpoint support, disable SQLite timing triggers for RAM authority and add recovery order, tombstone and outbox tables. This setup is not a runtime SQL access path.
TaskRecords 114 Describe task tables and derived indexes to the Controller's RecordRepository. Restore-time schema discovery preserves encoded-field/default contracts; change hooks maintain ordering, reverse dependencies, retention, timing and continuation capacity signals in the same publication.
TaskRecords.normalize 151 Capture immutable policies on task insertion. Normalize completion cycles only after READY; restoration preserves recorded clocks and permits explicit adoption of missing policies.
TaskRecords.changed 166 Maintain conversation activity, task timing/retention, native capacity wakes, stable task ordinals and ordered lookup trees after a row change. Update reverse dependency memberships and cancel/delete obsolete preparations and outbox records without invoking model or Gateway work.
copied 265 Return a detached mutable copy of a RAM row, preserving None for a missing record so callers can distinguish absence from an empty payload.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/memory_store.py

Python · Tier A

Store durable task intent, attempts and checkpoints on the Controller RAM authority. MemoryTaskStore joins lane, preparation, dependency and timing mixins; TaskRecords maintains indexes and checkpoint-recovery representation. Methods return detached validated models and publish related changes atomically, with explicit late-write tombstones and protected history pruning. Runtime SQL access is rejected; this store neither invokes models nor establishes that remote effects have settled.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
error 38 Build localized task-store conflicts while keeping the common LaneConflict type used by HTTP and coordinator callers.
MemoryTaskStore 45 Implement task intent, attempt/checkpoint history and retention on the shared Controller hub. Mixins supply lanes, dependencies, preparation and timing; runtime consumers receive detached models and cannot open a SQL compatibility connection.
MemoryTaskStore.db 60 Expose only the Records view bound to the current repository invocation. Access outside an operation has no implicit database connection.
MemoryTaskStore.atomic 73 Bind a supplied transaction or run a fresh optimistic publication, restoring any previous thread-local view even on failure. Callbacks can be retried by the hub and must not perform external effects.
MemoryTaskStore.create_task 170 Admit generic task intent, assign identity/title, register dependencies, prune eligible history and initialize parameter holds in one transaction. This creates durable intent, not a native run.
MemoryTaskStore.get_task 197 Read one trimmed task identity as a detached model. This low-level lookup can return retained archived rows; higher-level views apply visibility rules.
MemoryTaskStore.previous_task 203 Read the newest creation-sequence entry for one conversation, optionally reducing its context for display. It does not choose a queue predecessor from mutable display order.
MemoryTaskStore.get_task_by_request_id 213 Resolve a nonempty request through its latest recorded attempt and return that attempt’s task, or None when either is absent.
MemoryTaskStore.list_tasks 223 Filter indexed task candidates by lane, status, source and conversation, excluding deleted markers. Return 1–500 records ranked active/waiting/queued before history, with newest update first within each rank; archive inclusion is explicit.
MemoryTaskStore.update_task 269 Apply only supported clipped patch fields, optionally requiring the exact previous update timestamp. Reject moving dependency-linked tasks across conversations, ignore retired owners, stamp terminal completion and refresh lane/dependencies/runtime failure issues transactionally.
MemoryTaskStore.create_attempt 326 Create a request attempt only after Gateway-update, parameter-admission and task-retirement guards. Initialize start time for running status; the reservation/caller owns request uniqueness and task-current pointers.
MemoryTaskStore.get_attempt 356 Read a trimmed attempt identity as a detached validated model, preserving absence.
MemoryTaskStore.get_attempt_by_request_id 364 Choose the newest created attempt matching a trimmed request identity; return None for no recorded match.
MemoryTaskStore.chat_request_lineage 372 Join request bindings, attempts and tasks only when their identities agree, returning compact task/parent/mode/creation metadata. Retained bindings alone do not recreate deleted task lineage.
MemoryTaskStore.update_attempt 397 Patch an existing nonretired task attempt, clip display previews and fill first-start or terminal-completion times. Late updates for removed/retired owners return the existing projection without publishing.
MemoryTaskStore.list_attempts 433 Return the oldest 1–500 attempts for a task in creation order, with detached model validation.
MemoryTaskStore.add_checkpoint 444 Deduplicate by task/request/trace-event identity and reject deleted-task tombstones before storing clipped display fields and detached details. In the same transaction, let qualifying evidence update task-owned runtime issues; duplicate calls return None.
MemoryTaskStore.get_checkpoint 500 Read one checkpoint identity as a detached model with decoded detail.
MemoryTaskStore.list_checkpoints 508 Return the oldest 1–1,000 checkpoints ordered by creation time and trace event ID; this bounded history read is not a latest-events tail.
MemoryTaskStore.latest_checkpoint 520 Select the most recent checkpoint by creation time and event ID, or None for an empty task history.
MemoryTaskStore.latest_checkpoints 533 Collect existing latest checkpoints for nonblank requested task identities within one read view.
MemoryTaskStore.get_open_task 544 Select the most recently updated unarchived open task, optionally scoped to a lane. Unlike execution-capacity accounting, this projection can include admission-held work.
MemoryTaskStore.next_queued_task 558 Choose the first unarchived dependency-satisfied task in a lane after excluding Gateway update holds, using queue position then stable creation order. The eventual attempt still validates parameter and execution admission.
MemoryTaskStore.assert_dependencies_satisfied 582 Reevaluate the selected task’s dependency graph and fail closed unless it resolves to satisfied.
MemoryTaskStore.interrupt_active_tasks 590 Mark eligible non-chat work interrupted after restart, clear current ownership and refresh descendants. Preserve unstarted queue intent and clarification holds that have never acquired an attempt.
MemoryTaskStore.archive_task 630 Archive a generic task through the normal update path; positioned conversation tasks require their lane/conversation controls.
MemoryTaskStore.delete_task 673 Delete one existing task through the protected helper and report whether a row existed; validation failures abort the enclosing transaction.
MemoryTaskStore.delete_tasks 683 Delete requested task identities in one operation and return the number removed. A protected member raises and prevents partial publication.
MemoryTaskStore._prune 690 Consider only history older than the configured newest-task target, preserving active work, interrupted chat tasks, pending follow-ups/steers, lane blockers and referenced ancestors. Decide eligibility before deleting so one removal cannot expose an ancestor in this pass; the target is not a hard row cap.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/models.py

Python · Tier A

Define task creation, patches and persisted task/attempt/checkpoint views shared by API and repositories. Pydantic validates the public shapes, strict dependency selectors and input bounds; creation normalizes Gateway/Behavior Policy context. These records separate durable intent from request attempts and trace evidence. Runtime admission, dependencies, authority and execution remain with their owners; comments preserve all schema-producing docstrings and field declarations.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
AgentTaskCreate 39 Validate new task intent with strict dependency selectors, bounded prompt/identity fields and unknown-field rejection. The post-validator normalizes Gateway and Behavior Policy context; repository admission still owns dependencies, identity binding and execution readiness.
AgentTaskUpdate 86 Define the allowed optional task patch fields and preview bounds. Omitted fields remain untouched when repositories use exclude_unset; state-transition and ownership checks belong to the store.
TaskDependency 109 Represent an immutable top-level success prerequisite with its UI selection origin. Native activity dependencies and runtime satisfaction projections have separate models/owners.
AgentTaskRecord 122 Expose persisted intent, stable queue/creation order, dependency projection, request ownership and retained context/history. Status and timestamps are repository evidence; this schema alone does not authorize execution or infer external completion.
AgentTaskAttemptRecord 160 Represent one execution attempt and parent request within a durable task, including display previews and lifecycle times. Multiple attempts can preserve retry/continuation history without changing the task identity.
AgentTaskCheckpointRecord 182 Represent one trace-derived task checkpoint with source-event identity, compact display fields and structured detail. Repository deduplication and runtime-issue projection determine how repeated events are stored.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/preparation_compiler.py

Python · Tier A

Adapt the shared Task Contract compiler to an explicitly invoked queued-preparation session. QueuedCompilationSession copies accepted input/policy, owns inference budget and cancellation checks, routes safe events to task checkpoints and saves through the current SQL/RAM repository. prepare_task_contract claims the source before client creation and persists final outcomes without creating a native run, execution attempt or Gateway workload. Current production queue code consumes existing preparations but does not automatically call this generation helper. Client creation and ordinary compiler recovery can make model calls when an internal caller invokes it.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
QueuedCompilationSession 32 Adapt the ordinary compiler protocol to a private queued-intent record without constructing an AgentLoop, native execution store or Gateway. The task repository owns durable state and the supplied client factory owns inference configuration; this session provides budget, cancellation, events and source-checked saves.
QueuedCompilationSession.transaction 107 Enter the standalone task-store lock and immediate SQL transaction. Active RAM paths use repository methods instead; this context never wraps provider transport.
QueuedCompilationSession.save 115 Delegate RAM saves to atomic source revalidation, or reuse the active SQL acceptance connection before opening a fresh transaction. Persist partial attempts and optional final outcome through the existing preparation owner.
QueuedCompilationSession.event 135 Record local compiler metrics and project safe event detail. Qualifying runtime issues become deterministic task checkpoints in the active SQL transaction or a separate RAM publication; an optional sink receives projected detail afterward.
QueuedCompilationSession.cancel_requested 190 Observe explicit budget cancellation or task removal/archive/cancellation through current store state. A queued task remains separate from the private compiler running status.
QueuedCompilationSession.source_changed 198 Ask the backend owner whether the accepted generating source remains current. Use a RAM snapshot or standalone SQL transaction; no inference runs during this check.
QueuedCompilationSession.cancel 206 Mark the private compiler outcome cancelled and save its state. Final preparation lifecycle publication remains with the normal finished save.
QueuedCompilationSession.checkpoint 212 Before more compiler work, persist cancellation or stale-source state and report that processing should stop. An unchanged current source continues through the ordinary compiler.
QueuedCompilationSession.call 225 Check inference budget/cancellation before invoking the supplied operation. Attempt reservation already belongs to the shared compiler; response acceptance must independently revalidate source ownership.
QueuedCompilationSession.acceptance 235 For SQL, hold a source-checked writer transaction and route nested saves into it, clearing the temporary connection in all exits. For RAM, yield a current snapshot check and rely on atomic save to recheck identity; no SQL lock spans model transport.
prepare_task_contract 252 Claim one server-owned source revision and invoke the shared compiler with a client built from a detached accepted context. Existing/disabled records skip client construction; an ordinary mismatched client model fails unless model routing is present. Persist projected factory/compiler failures and the final record without inventing a substitute model or hidden retry. This entry point does not automatically schedule queued work.

src/agent_runtime/tasks/preparation_models.py

Python · Tier A

Define the private durable TaskPreparation record and accepted-source identity used by both store backends. The record separates compilation lifecycle, source revision, model/prompt provenance, attempt state and first consumption from task execution status. preparation_identity hashes only compiler-relevant accepted input and snapshots, so queue reorder or dependency outcomes do not replace intent. Storage and authenticated import enforce transitions and authority; these shapes do not invoke inference or execute tools.

Significant symbols

Python · Tier A

Project task or individual-request wall time from persisted lifecycle and compact trace receipts. project sweeps clipped intervals into waiting, active, thinking, execution, overlap and unmeasured categories without counting parallel work twice. project_request excludes ancestors; advance extrapolates only the current category of a running payload. It starts no timer, replays no event journal and does not infer execution success or internal model reasoning.
